gen-fs-nippo-gf-blinker: Blinker reads easily, its lowercase filling most of the line's height. Strokes hold their thickness and the openings stay wide, so paragraphs keep moving, while Nippo adds wire-cut, technical edge above.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-georama: Nippo stands up with small letters nearly capital-sized, every stroke cut like wire. And Georama, a friendly sans with barely rising capitals, lets paragraphs unroll smoothly down the page.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-gidole: Wire-cut and technical up top, then Gidole below, drawn like neon tube. And Nippo does its finest work when it's given a few words to say at generous size.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-heebo: Heebo gives text a deep central band, its curves stopping short instead of closing in. Heebo would crowd out Nippo if the heading were made small, because Nippo draws a steady line with no pressure variation.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-hind-guntur: Hind Guntur draws stamped-metal lowercase with wide gaps between curve ends and stems, every stroke like a steel cable outline. Nippo grabs attention; Hind Guntur carries the reading.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-hind-mysuru: Hind Mysuru keeps its lowercase pressed close to the ascender height. Nippo adds wire-cut, technical lettering above it, and the two read as one steady, contemporary system without calligraphic thinning anywhere.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-huninn: Huninn is modern and businesslike, its lowercase rising close to cap height. Huninn feels sturdy and level next to Nippo, whose small letters stand almost as tall as capitals.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-karla: Karla reads stocky and friendly, its middle band running deep. Paragraphs feel sturdy and approachable, while Nippo up top keeps a round bowl whose outline never swells or thins.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-khula: Khula reads soft and level, curves holding their mouths open. Long paragraphs would settle into a squat, brush-pen belly of text, while Nippo above keeps every stroke uniform, cut like wire.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-kufam: Contemporary and clean, Kufam draws like neon sign tube. Nippo does its best work in technical, wire-cut headings, while Kufam carries running text with generously open curves in e.
